New Verbs

Overnight applications of the pin (xswap checkpoint, sigma=0, carrot on): pace as a commandable dial, and two motion programs — orbit and figure-8 — that exist in zero training demonstrations, flown at 8-10 cm fidelity from displacement words alone.

the tempo verb — same route, three commanded speeds

drag to orbit · wheel to zoom · shift-drag to pan

Identical 4-point sketch, resampled at 0.6x / 1.0x / 1.5x demo speed. Realized crossing times: 88 / 53 / 37 steps — gains 0.60 and 1.43 against commanded 0.6 and 1.5. Pace is a near-unit-gain command dial. All 15 flights 5/5 judge; note the clearance cost off-tempo (0/5 clean at both extremes vs 2/5 at 1.0x) — the flow's crossing finesse is tuned at demo pace.

the orbit — 1.5 loops around the gate (zero demos contain an orbit)

drag to orbit · wheel to zoom · shift-drag to pan

Five flights, 100% arc completion, tracking median 0.07-0.10 m, all clearance-clean. The judge's 'fail' is expected — orbiting crosses the aperture plane repeatedly by design. A behavior class absent from every training demo, composed entirely from displacement words.

the figure-8 — sustained curvature reversal in open space

drag to orbit · wheel to zoom · shift-drag to pan

Two opposite-handed lobes: the hardest shape to speak in prefix-sum words. 100% completion, 0.09 m median tracking, clean.
